b: While I prefer to focus on experiences over things for gift giving, books are an exception. They are a thing but they are also an experience. See below for a list of beautiful books for gifting.

There are so many ways to give gifts to book lovers. You can give them a gift card to their favorite local book store. Gift them a membership to Libro.fm (more below on why I prefer and recommend Libro.fm) if they love listen to books and share them. One year, my daughter gave me a basket of 12 wrapped books. They were each marked with something like, “read for creative inspiration” or “read this for an uplifting story about women” so throughout the year, I could choose a book that fit exactly what I was looking for.

When you consider books for gifting, remember what format your book lover prefers (audio, digital or paper book). Consider leaving a note in the book about why you thought this would be a good book for them. This may be better than actually writing in the book because then they can easily pass it on when they are done. Who knows, it might even come back to you!
The synopsis for each book comes from StoryGraph (the app I use to track my reading). Use these books for gifting, enjoying and hopefully sharing.
1. The Little Shop of Merry and Bright by Jenny Bayliss
I am looking forward to my annual holiday book from Jenny Bayliss. Any of her books would be a lovely gift this time of year.

Three years ago, Casey declined her boyfriend’s marriage proposal . . . and it went viral. After years of dealing with the backlash online, Casey now leads a quiet life, working as a stock replenisher for a family-owned department store. No risk of public humiliation, no stress, no possibility of love.

Until she meets the Spirit of Christmas Present, Margo, who has chosen to sit this holiday out. Margo offers Casey a bargain: She will use her powers to erase the video that made Casey notorious. There’s just one catch. Casey must witness five of her alternate realities, and if after all five she still wants it wiped, Margo will grant her wish. While glimpses into other lifetimes are fascinating, the question remains: What if everything Casey wants is waiting for her in the life she already has? Amazon | Libro.fm | Bookshop.org
2. Project 333, The Minimalist Fashion Challenge That Proves Less Really Is So Much More by Courtney Carver

This would make a great gift for your friend who is ready to pare down. If you are curious, offer to do the challenge with them! Project 333 promises that not only can you survive with just 33 items in your closet for 3 months, but you’ll thrive just like the thousands of woman who have taken on the challenge and never looked back. Let the de-cluttering begin

As Carver reveals in this book, once we finally release ourselves from the cyclical nature of consumerism and focus less on our shoes and more on our self-care, we not only look great we feel great– and we can see a clear path to make other important changes in our lives that reach far beyond our closets. With tips, solutions, and a closet-full of inspiration, this life-changing minimalist manual shows readers that we are so much more than what we wear, and that who we are and what we have is so much more than enough. Amazon | Libro.fm | Bookshop.org
3. The Nice Life, How To Elevate The Everyday and Find Joy in What You Have by Rachel Wilkerson Miller

I read an early copy of this book and knew it would be at the top of my list of books for gifting. This book is a refreshing, joyful invitation to cultivate a life that feels abundant, sumptuous, and deeply satisfying. Despite all that is wrong, you can still have a nice life.

A nice life is cozy, it’s comfortable, it’s meaningful. It’s filled with moments of beauty. It’s for anyone interested in the #softlife trend. You can have a nice life even when facing illness, grief, or unemployment; when you’re stressed about work, politics, or climate change. Living well in hard times can be an act of resistance and self-love. How do we get there? By making an effort and living with intention. Amazon | Libro.fm | Bookshop.org
You know those books that you never want to end, this is one of them. This is the best book I’ve read all year.

When Daphne Fuller and her husband Jonathan visit the Metropolitan Museum of Art, they notice an older, white-haired gentleman following them. The man turns out to be Eddie Triplett, her former stepfather, who had been married to her mother for a little more than year when Daphne was nine. Now fifty-three, Daphne hasn’t seen Eddie for many years, not since the fateful event that changed the direction of both their lives. Meeting again, time falls away; while their relationship was brief, it had a profound impact on them both, and now that they are reunited, they have no intention of ever being separated again. Amazon | Libro.fm | Bookshop.org
5. A Short Guide to a Happy Life by Anna Quindlen

In this treasure of a book, Anna Quindlen, the bestselling novelist and columnist, reflects on what it takes to “get a life”–to live deeply every day and from your own unique self, rather than merely to exist through your days. “Knowledge of our own mortality is the greatest gift God ever gives us,” Quindlen writes, “because unless you know the clock is ticking, it is so easy to waste our days, our lives.”

Her mother died when Quindlen was nineteen: “It was the dividing line between seeing the world in black and white, and in Technicolor. The lights came on for the darkest possible reason. . . . I learned something enduring, in a very short period of time, about life. And that was that it was glorious, and that you had no business taking it for granted.” But how to live from that perspective, to fully engage in our days? In A Short Guide to a Happy Life, Quindlen guides us with an understanding that comes from knowing how to see the view, the richness in living. Amazon | Libro.fm | Bookshop.org
6. Keep Moving: Notes on Loss, Creativity, and Change by Maggie Smith

For fans of Cheryl Strayed and Anne Lamott, a collection of quotes and essays on facing life’s challenges with creativity, courage, and resilience.
When Maggie Smith, the award-winning author of the viral poem “Good Bones,” started writing inspirational daily Twitter posts in the wake of her divorce, they unexpectedly caught fire. In this deeply moving book of quotes and essays, Maggie writes about new beginnings as opportunities for transformation. Like kintsugi, the Japanese art of mending broken ceramics with gold, Keep Moving celebrates the beauty and strength on the other side of loss. This is a book for anyone who has gone through a difficult time and is wondering: What comes next? Amazon | Libro.fm | Bookshop.org
7. The Creative Act: A Way of Being by Rick Rubin
Creativity has a place in everyone’s life, and everyone can make that place larger. In fact, there are few more important responsibilities.

The Creative Act is a beautiful and generous course of study that illuminates the path of the artist as a road we all can follow. It distills the wisdom gleaned from a lifetime’s work into a luminous reading experience that puts the power to create moments—and lifetimes—of exhilaration and transcendence within closer reach for all of us. Amazon | Libro.fm | Bookshop.org

More on why I use and recommend Libro.fm for audiobooks.

I listen to audiobooks with Libro.fm for a few reasons. For starters, you get a couple of free audiobooks when you sign up with Libro.fm. Next, you can choose a local bookstore to support with each order. And, Libro.fm allows you to download your books, unlike Audible where you have to listen to them on the platform. Because you can download your audiobooks, you can share them with friends. When friends share their audiobooks with me, I listen with an app called Book Player. I’m sure there are other options!
